deng-2026-preprint.citation: Deng, Wu, Glenn and He (2026), Tropical cyclones intensify mesoscale eddy variability and accelerate Western Boundary Current instability, EarthArXiv preprint.
deng-2026-preprint.access: Author preprint indexed primary full text reviewed, especially the model detachment discussion and Supplementary Figure S2 caption. June 2026 preprint, not peer-reviewed. Original PDF and figure retrieval returned HTTP 403; original bytes, figure pixels and raw model fields not verified. Only explicit simulated event dates and their calendar-day differences admitted.

records.source_locator: Supplementary Figure S2 caption, supporting-information lines 20–26; main-text LCE Edison detachment discussion, manuscript lines 179–184; event-identification methods, lines 346–356.
records.case_label: Edison model event-date contrast: No-Hurricane versus Control
records.period_label: Different simulated worlds: Control detachment 2024-10-10; No-Hurricane detachment 2024-10-16; not an observed elapsed life interval
records.definition: Calendar-day difference between the simulated No-Hurricane detachment date and the simulated Control detachment date for the source-named Edison case.
records.scope: One named simulated October 2024 event. CNAPS2-derived regional ocean model; forcing-removal contrast, not an observed temporal change within a single eddy.
records.qualification: Preprint result from indexed primary text; full original methods, figure pixels and raw fields not independently reviewed. Removing Helene and Milton yields this source-reported event-date difference in this model. Separate contrasts are not additive and are not pooled into an uncertainty range. Model detachment criteria are not transferred to observed front measurements. Date agreement with registry initial separation does not verify physical identity. No eddy lifespan, residence time, size, annual range or observed hurricane causal effect inferred.
